target_customer: US consumers who need glasses or contact lens prescription renewals and eye screening at home
problem: Eye exams are hard to access, and preventable blindness persists; the company aimed for a fully online eye exam.
business_model: Consumer telehealth fees per exam (prescription renewal about 30 dollars, doctor chat about 55 dollars per Product Hunt)

founders.name: Quinn Wang
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a recovering cataract surgeon.

founders.name: Kristine Hara
founders.background_notes: YC page: engineer number 6 at UnitedMasters and a computational biologist.

technical_complexity.rationale: Remote eye exams need validated vision tests and deep learning with regulatory and clinical risk; YC page cites patentable deep tech.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical validation and patents could help, but unproven at this stage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents already offered online prescription renewal tests; no source on effect on Quadrant Eye.

market_need_then: YC page cites a 137 billion dollar eye health market; no dated demand evidence beyond that.
outcome_analysis: Quadrant Eye was a four person online eye exam startup that raised only a small seed and is listed Inactive. No shutdown post or press explains the cause, so it is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503. The 130K seed rests on CB Insights; another directory says 125K. Competitor search found Warby Parker, Visibly and 1-800 Contacts coverage but no source dated near 2021, so the list is empty. A CB Insights acquired label belongs to a comparison page about Easee, not Quadrant Eye.
